newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond mart expects new debt avalanche.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond mart expects new debt avalanche.

text.p: An improved interest rate environment is expected to trigger an avalanche of new debt offerings as U.S. corporations capitalize on lower financing costs, dealers said.
"There's a slew of new names out there," said one syndicate source. "The calendar is certainly building."

Among large debt offerings expected to hit the market near-term are CSX Corp's $2.0 billion multi-tranche debt offering. The deal is expected to include five-year, seven-year, 10-year and 30-year tranches, source said.
The deal, is also expected to include a 30-year trust preferred securities tranche, sources added.
Among other rumored deals is a mega mult-tranche debt offering from Norfolk Southern Corp of between $3.0 and $4.0 billion, sources said.

Another $900 million in a two-part debt offering is expected to come from Banc One Corp. The deal is expected to include $400 million of a 10-year noncallable debt and $500 million of a 30-year noncallable issue, sources said.
Also, Kroger Co may set $200 million in debt via Goldman Sachs & Co, sources added.
Barrick Gold Corp is expected to set $500 million in a 10-year issue via Goldman Sachs. Price talk on the issue is 60 basis points over Treasuries, dealers said.

Transocean Offshore Iinc is expected to tap the market as well with a Baa1/A rated $300 million two-part debt offering including a $200 million of 30-year bond and $100 million of a 30-year, putable in 10-years, issue via Goldman Sachs.
Among yankee debt offerings, Malaysian electric utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd will bring $500 million of a 10-year yankee bond via UBS Securities, sources said.

Meanwhile, as the tone in the market remains improved those issuers still pondering whether to finance debt now or later, may be prompted to do so now, ahead of next months meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting arm.
In March, the Federal Open Market Committe voted to tighten credit and boosted the key overnight lending rate by 25 basis points; therefore, increasing the costs of borrowing for U.S. corporations.
Many deals were later postponed as interest rates shot up, dealer said.
Prior to the Fed's decision to hike the federal funds rate, the benchmark 30-year bond was trading at a 6.92 percent, a week ago the bond traded as high as 7.17 percent, but now sits at 7.08 percent.
"Issuers are more likely to get their financing done now while the environment for them remains favorable," said another syndicate source.
Turning to the high-yield arena, L-3 Communications is expected to issue $200 million in 144A senior subordinated noted due 2007 via Lehman Brothers.
Other names in the pipeline are Telex Communications and Colorado Prime Corp, soruces said.
Later this week, Neenah Corp is expected to issue $140 million 144-A senior subordinated notes due 2007 via Chase Securities.
Additionally, KSL Recreation Group Inc is expected to issue $125 million 144-A senior subordinated notes due 2007.
